rationale: The staging flag for going live, and nothing more. The worker is contract-locked to production_no_live (mode string, activation file and runtime config all three), so flipping this does not and cannot place an order; it records the operator's intent, the station allowlist the first live batch is limited to, and travels into the go-live migration as its input. The migration that mints the live contract must refuse to run while live_enabled is false.
allowlist_note: Every station with book history that is not barred (45 - 15 = 30), operator ruling 2026-08-30. Replaces the eight-station 2026-08-28 batch, which was measured to carry no selection skill over this same set: it returned +33.3% against +23.2%, but drawing eight stations at random from these thirty matched or beat that 21.6% of the time (p=0.216), and it was stale -- KLGA and KSFO both scored 5/5 and were absent while KORD sat on it with three chains. The bar is what carries the value (fleet +1.4% -> unbarred +23.2%, and the hand-picked bar held fixed across a nine-day walk-forward returned +15.6 points at p=0.001); narrowing further past it is not supported. Thirty stations also run at the lowest daily volatility of the candidates (55 points against 83 for the eight) and deploy 69.3 USDC a day against 24.5. Day-one size is controlled by portfolio_risk_fraction, not by shortening this list. LLBG/LTFM/UUWW are excluded on purpose: the fleet roster moved to 48 in another session's working tree, but those three have never produced a position or a settlement, so they cannot be part of a live batch.
